answer.rationale: With the contract lapsing in 14 days, no auto-renew, and the line already at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, a primary-vendor switch or dropping coverage carries unacceptable delivery risk in this window. The incumbent has explicitly refused to reopen price this cycle, so memory_c4's renegotiation pattern may not transfer here — I want the archived record on c4 to see whether that recovery came from leverage conditions (e.g., competitive bids, timing) that don't hold now. I also want to re-verify c1 since it's the core justification for renewal-as-safe-default, to confirm it wasn't a survivorship-biased account that omitted cost drift. Given the time constraint, I intend to renew the incumbent short-term to protect delivery continuity, while attempting to structure the renewal around a multi-year volume commitment (per c6's logic) as a lever for cost reduction rather than spot price concession, since spot price is foreclosed. This does not fully satisfy the 18% finance mandate, so I'm flagging that gap explicitly rather than assuming this decision resolves it — second-sourcing (c3) and vendor-switch cost savings (c2) remain unaddressed and should be the priority for next cycle's single decision slot.
